name: Glass Dusk
texts: A bar under the greeting: every game played in the last two weeks, as wide as its share of the hours and in its own colours. Point at a part to see the game and its hours; a click opens it.
A small line under each number: installed, in how many games, average completion, drives.
Achievement progress of the game on the Continue card.
Behind the Shift+Tab panels: a light veil or Steam's dark sheet.

Big art: the focused game's art, sharp, across the whole first screen with the carousel at its foot, as in Steam's Big Art Mode, whether or not that setting of Steam's (Settings → Home) is on. Steam's: the layout is left to that setting, over the theme's softened art.
Colour of buttons and highlights. Game art: the colours of the game in view, and with none in view (store, community) the last one's. Fixed uses Accent from the Colors tab.
Cover: the focused game's art fills the screen and lends its colour.
Every game in the library, installed or not.
Game Overview, browser and toolbar: smoked glass or Steam's own.
Hours played in the last two weeks.
How strongly the game art shows through.

Left alone on the library, Steam becomes the art of the game in view, with its logo, the time and the date; the first move brings everything back. Never while something is downloading or a video is playing.
Millennium plugins that draw their own interface (HLTB for Steam, Achievement Groups, Player Count, Extendium): in the theme's colours, or as the plugin ships them.
Opening another game: the accent flows from the old colour to the new one and the art behind the glass fades over. Instant changes both at once.
Point at a cover in the recently played row: a card with the game's screenshots, its name and hours. The store's screenshots are fetched from Steam at that moment.
Smoked glass over the art of the game you have open: the client takes its accent colour from that art. Styles the library, store, menus, Big Picture and the in-game overlay.
Space taken in Steam's library folders, in GB.
Steam's What's New shelf on the library home.
Steam's row for adding a shelf to the library home.
Text the theme draws itself: home header, Big Picture chip, dates.

The account chooser when Steam starts (Who's playing?): the art of the game you played last, the covers of your own games drifting past, the art of your games one after another, plain dusk or Steam's wall of covers, each with the theme's glass, or Steam's own look. It shows only if Steam asks which account to use.
The balance in the top bar. Blurred, it shows when you point at it.
The collections a game is in, shown at the top right of its art on the game page, as Steam does. A click opens the collection.
The focused game's numbers under the carousel, beside Steam's own label: time played, last played, achievements.
The row of recently played games under the Continue card.
The surface of the glass panels: a fine grain, and the edges that face the light lit in the accent. Plain is the smooth glass of earlier versions.
The theme's header (greeting, stats, Continue) or Steam's shelves only.
Two-tone takes a second colour from the game art, close to the first and as bright, and runs the main buttons and the progress bars from one to the other. Solid is one colour.
Where the Continue card and the recently played row take their games: only what is installed on this machine, or everything in the library.

Your game list beside the store and other web pages of the main window: off, pinned there, coming out when you point at the window's edge, or a rail of your last games' covers that opens into the list.
